jamie_customer: Hey team — our Android app (SDK v1.4.2) drops the SSE stream when switching from office WiFi to cellular. App sees a partial JSON chunk and then the connection closes. Happens ~3/10 times. Any quick triage steps?

alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the client logs and a short repro? Also which carrier / Android version?

jamie_customer: Android 12, carrier: AT&T. Repro steps I used: connect to WiFi, start streaming long response (~2k tokens), toggle WiFi off (phone switches to 4G). Attached trimmed log:```
I/StreamClient: open() -> connected, lat=120ms
I/StreamClient: recv: {"partial":"Hello world","chunk_id":42}
W/Network: network change detected: WIFI -> CELLULAR
E/StreamClient: recv error: java.net.SocketException: Connection reset
I/StreamClient: close() code=1006
```

morgan_oncall: Thanks. That pattern looks like a TCP RST after NAT rebind. Do you have a pcap or server logs? If no pcap, try a quick tcpdump on client while reproing.

jamie_customer: I ran a short tcpdump. Relevant lines:```
IP 10.11.12.13.54321 > 54.123.45.67.443: Flags [.], ack 12345, win 64240, length 0
IP 54.123.45.67.443 > 10.11.12.13.54321: Flags [R], seq 98765, win 0, length 0  # server sent RST
```

alex_support: Server RST suggests the server closed the connection, possibly because the mux mapping for that client socket expired on our edge when the client re-IP'd. Do you see any auth errors?

jamie_customer: No auth error. Token still valid, we tried immediate reconnect and got 401 once (token refresh race) but mostly 200 then immediate close.

sara_devex: Quick mitigation for Android clients: enable more aggressive keepalives on the client (e.g., send a small ping every 10s) and enable automatic resume with KV cache so partial output can continue. Also add jitter to reconnect backoff to avoid thundering herd.

lee_runtime: For engineering: the edge currently garbage-collects inactive TLS sessions after 30s of no activity; when client switches networks the NAT rebind makes it look inactive. Two options: 1) extend the edge idle TTL for long-lived SSE to 60s for premium routes, or 2) server proactively pings client once network-change signal is suspected (we can infer from TCP FIN/RST patterns).

alex_support: Jamie — can you try the client change and report? Steps: 1) set keepalive/ping interval to 10s, 2) enable resume.kv_cache=true, 3) set reconnect.backoff initial=200ms,max=2s with jitter. Also try toggling `useHttp2PriorKnowledge=false` in the SDK (we saw issues with some carriers long-lived h2 connections).

jamie_customer: Will try tomorrow AM and report. Curious about billing: if stream aborts mid-response, are we billed for tokens sent before the abort?

alex_support: Short answer: yes — tokens emitted by the model are billed; partial responses that were delivered count. If the client reconnects and resumes, only new tokens are billed. I'll include a note for billing team if you want a special credit for this run.

morgan_oncall: Action items: 1) jamie to try client config and post outcome, 2) eng to evaluate extending idle TTL for SSE on premium routes (lee assigned), 3) docs: add a short triage guide for mobile keepalive/network-change (sara assigned).

deploybot: [automated] created ticket RI-1548 (edge-idle-ttl) for runtime follow-up.

jamie_customer: Thanks — I'll update once I have repro results. :thumbsup:
